summary: Downtown Printing Center is a single-location print shop at 46 Paterson St. in downtown New Brunswick, operating since 1977 and selling digital and offset printing, screen-printed apparel, signs and banners, plus binding, Western Union and passport photos to local businesses, Rutgers-area customers and walk-ins. Its web front door is a bare GoDaddy site (logo, one stock press photo, © 2022) whose only intake is a phone number or a free-text Name/Email/Message form with no quote fields, file upload or online ordering, and its Google rating is middling at 3.7. Public records add a compliance dimension: a 2016 NJ consent order terminated its authorization to print state prescription blanks after verification failures, and it is absent from the state's current approved-vendor list.

facts.fact: Located at 46 Paterson St., New Brunswick, NJ 08901; phone (732) 246-7990, fax (732) 246-3425; store hours shown as 8:30 am - 5:30 pm on the day of the check.

The shop states it has served New Brunswick and neighboring cities since 1977 and is in the downtown district near the Middlesex County Courthouse, Robert Wood Johnson Hospital and Rutgers University.

Services page lists four families - digital (color/B&W copies, large and small runs, posters, engineering prints), offset (raised printing, business cards, flyers/postcards, letterheads, envelopes, booklets, brochures, menus, manuals), screen (t-shirts, sweatshirts, hoodies) and signs (lawn, vehicle, banners, A-frames) - plus binding/finishing, Western Union and passport photos.

Google business profile: name 'Downtown Printing Center', category 'Print shop', 3.7 stars, 46 Paterson St., 'Closed - Opens 8:30 AM Mon', website downtownprint.com, phone (732) 246-7990; a separate 'Western Union' money-transfer listing is shown inside the same address on Floor 1.

2016 NJ Division of Consumer Affairs final consent order terminated the shop's authorization as a New Jersey prescription-blank (NJPB) vendor after it filled orders totalling 15,000+ blanks in the names of people who were not licensed NJ physicians, without verifying licensure, identity or address of record; the order names Juan Ruiz as Owner/President and sets re-application, audit and material-destruction conditions.

Downtown Printing Center does not appear on the NJ Division of Consumer Affairs' current published list of printer vendors approved to print and sell New Jersey prescription blanks (an 11-page vendor table; the PDF text carries no visible date, though the search listing labels it 'Updated 07/10/2026').

At 390 px phone width the home page is a hamburger menu, the logo ('over 40 years', 'since 1977', digital/offset/screen/signs), one stock press photo and a '© 2022' GoDaddy footer - no address, phone, hours, service copy or call/quote button as text; the page title is just the business name, with no meta description and no h1.

The contact page offers two clickable tel: links (732-246-7990 and the fax line) and a single Name/Email/Message form whose submit button is 'SEND', protected by reCAPTCHA; it publishes no email address and no quote fields, quantities, turnaround or artwork upload.
There is no careers page (https://downtownprint.com/careers returns HTTP 404), and the site nav is only Home / Services / About Us / Contact.

A Birdeye mirror of Google review data shows 3.8 stars from 29 reviews with the profile 'not claimed by the business owner', and lists weekday hours as 9:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m. - an hour later than the shop's own site.

A 1990 NJBiz Central Jersey fax/phone directory entry lists Downtown Printing Center at 46 Paterson St. with business type 'Printing/Linotronic Output/Public Fax', corroborating decades at the same address.

A directory profile describes the shop as established in 1977, providing service throughout the state, offering full-service printing plus screen printing, signs, Western Union and passport photos, and notes street parking only.

operations_signals: Intake is phone or a free-text Name/Email/Message form - no quote request with size, quantity, stock, deadline or artwork upload, and no online ordering; no email address is published on the site (https://downtownprint.com/contact)

Hours are Mon-Fri 8:30-17:30 with Saturday and Sunday zeroed out in the LocalBusiness schema, so every job is quoted and produced inside a single weekday shift with no stated after-hours coverage (https://downtownprint.com/contact)

Hours conflict across listings: own site and schema say 8:30-5:30, while the Birdeye/Google mirror says 9:00-6:00 - customers arriving 5:30-6:00 may find it closed (https://reviews.birdeye.com/downtown-printing-center-inc-552901184)

Front-desk work is interrupt-driven: alongside print jobs the counter handles Western Union money transfers and passport photos, and Google lists the Western Union service inside the same address on Floor 1 (https://www.google.com/maps/search/Downtown+Printing+Center+46+Paterson+St+New+Brunswick+NJ)
Store hours are only stated as 'open today' text on the contact page with no calendar or booking system, so a customer cannot self-schedule a pickup or press check (https://downtownprint.com/contact)

Service area claimed as the whole state in a directory description, but the physical operation is one street-level counter in downtown New Brunswick with street parking only (https://www.loc8nearme.com/new-jersey/new-brunswick/downtown-printing-center/5678333/)

Regulated printing used to be part of the workflow: the 2016 consent order documents a manual NJPB ordering process with signature, license-status and address-of-record verification steps that the shop failed to perform (https://www.nj.gov/oag/newsreleases16/Downtown-Printing_Final-Consent-Order.pdf)
hiring_signals: No current or recent job posting found for the shop: searches of Indeed, ZipRecruiter and Glassdoor returned no listing, and the website has no careers page (https://downtownprint.com/careers)
No job-related pages, no 'now hiring' notice and no staff page anywhere in the site's four-page nav (https://downtownprint.com/)

Absence of postings is itself a signal that the shop is not publicising roles - inference: staff are likely hired through the counter/network rather than job boards (https://downtownprint.com/contact)
review_themes: Google rating is mid-range: 3.7 stars as shown on the signed-out Maps profile, and 3.8 from 29 reviews on the Birdeye mirror - a mixed rather than poor reputation (https://www.google.com/maps/search/Downtown+Printing+Center+46+Paterson+St+New+Brunswick+NJ)

Most recent review visible (July 2026) praises counter staff as helpful and efficient and able to handle 'whatever printing needs' (https://www.loc8nearme.com/new-jersey/new-brunswick/downtown-printing-center/5678333/)

Positive theme around quality and timeliness of event printing: a 2022 reviewer describes wedding printing as beautiful and timely (https://www.loc8nearme.com/new-jersey/new-brunswick/downtown-printing-center/5678333/)

Positive theme around the Western Union counter: a 2023 reviewer thanks a named staff member for being professional, kind and patient (https://www.loc8nearme.com/new-jersey/new-brunswick/downtown-printing-center/5678333/)

Only three recent reviews were readable on the aggregator, with a 'more comments' link returning HTTP 403 and no review text at all on the signed-out Google view, so complaint themes (wait times, responsiveness, pricing) could not be verified (https://www.loc8nearme.com/new-jersey/new-brunswick/downtown-printing-center/5678333/)
tech_footprint: Website is GoDaddy Website Builder output, copyright 2022, four pages, no meta description, no h1 on the home page and a page title that is only the business name (https://downtownprint.com/)

LocalBusiness JSON-LD is present with the street address, geo coordinates (40.494972, -74.444656) and Mon-Fri 08:30-17:30 opening hours, but it is not backed by readable service or address text on the home page (https://downtownprint.com/)

Only widget on the site is a reCAPTCHA-protected GoDaddy contact form; no live chat, no booking calendar, no CRM, no customer portal, no e-commerce checkout and no file-upload tool (https://downtownprint.com/contact)
No social profiles linked anywhere in the page markup - the only outbound links are Google's reCAPTCHA policy pages and GoDaddy (https://downtownprint.com/contact)
No prices, samples, brochure or downloadable content published; services are communicated as a flat bullet list on one page rather than per-product pages (https://downtownprint.com/services)
robots.txt is only 'User-agent: *' with no rules, so nothing blocks crawlers or AI agents (https://downtownprint.com/robots.txt)
growth_signals: No evidence of expansion found in this pass: one address since at least 1990, no new-location or acquisition news, no awards or press coverage in local outlets (https://njbiz.com/the-fax-network/)
Branding leans entirely on tenure - 'over 40 years' and 'since 1977' are baked into the logo image rather than into service or offer messaging (https://downtownprint.com/)

Service mix has broadened beyond printing into counter services (Western Union money transfer, passport photos), which Google lists as a separate entity inside the address - a way to keep walk-in traffic during print lulls (https://www.google.com/maps/search/Downtown+Printing+Center+46+Paterson+St+New+Brunswick+NJ)

One revenue line was removed rather than added: the NJPB prescription-blank vending authorization was terminated in 2016 for a minimum of three years pending audits, and the shop is absent from the current approved list (https://www.nj.gov/oag/newsreleases16/Downtown-Printing_Final-Consent-Order.pdf)

An unclaimed review profile (Birdeye flags it as not claimed by the owner) suggests no one is actively managing reputation or responding to reviews (https://reviews.birdeye.com/downtown-printing-center-inc-552901184)
physical_signals: Single street-level storefront at 46 Paterson St., New Brunswick; directory lists street parking only, with the Middlesex County Courthouse, Robert Wood Johnson Hospital and Rutgers nearby (https://www.loc8nearme.com/new-jersey/new-brunswick/downtown-printing-center/5678333/)
Production happens on site across digital, offset/raised-print, screen-print and sign workflows, with binding and finishing on the service list (https://downtownprint.com/services)

The only equipment image on the site is a generic stock press photo hosted by GoDaddy, not a picture of their own machines, so the actual press/equipment inventory is unknown (https://downtownprint.com/)

Google lists the Western Union desk as 'Floor 1' of the same address, indicating a multi-use retail floor rather than a dedicated plant (https://www.google.com/maps/search/Downtown+Printing+Center+46+Paterson+St+New+Brunswick+NJ)

Customer-supplied photos exist on the Loc8NearMe gallery (storefront/interior), but no square footage, seat count, dock or fleet information is published anywhere found (https://www.loc8nearme.com/new-jersey/new-brunswick/downtown-printing-center/5678333/)
decision_maker: Juan Ruiz, Owner/President - named as Owner and President of Downtown Printing Center in the 2016 NJ Division of Consumer Affairs final consent order (https://www.nj.gov/oag/newsreleases16/Downtown-Printing_Final-Consent-Order.pdf). Not confirmed as current; no owner or team is named on the shop's own website.

inferences.inference: Every job is re-keyed by a person at the counter because the only digital intake is a free-text message box.
inferences.reasoning: The contact form has fields for name, email and message only - no size, quantity, stock, deadline or artwork upload - so staff must re-enter specs into whatever estimating or job-ticket system they use; no such system is visible on the site.

inferences.inference: The shop has a manual-verification compliance gap that an agent could close if it re-enters regulated printing.
inferences.reasoning: The 2016 consent order lists five specific verification failures (original prescriber signature, active license, identity of the person ordering and picking up, address of record) on 15,000+ blanks; nothing on the current website suggests any structured order-verification intake exists today.

inferences.inference: Likely a very small team (roughly 2-10 people).
inferences.reasoning: One storefront, four-page website, no careers page or postings, no named staff page and mid-range review volume; a third-party firmographic page estimating 2-10 employees is consistent with this but appears auto-generated and was not verified.

inferences.inference: Missed calls and after-hours inquiries are probably lost rather than captured.
inferences.reasoning: The business is open 8:30-5:30 weekdays only, publishes no email address, offers no form auto-reply or booking, and its hours are inconsistent across listings - an after-hours web visitor has no self-serve path to a price or a callback commitment.

inferences.inference: Demand is seasonal and deadline-driven around the university and courthouse.
inferences.reasoning: The About page positions the shop next to Rutgers, the county courthouse and the hospital, and the service list skews to event printing (wedding work in reviews), apparel and signs - work that clusters around semester starts, elections, weddings and filing deadlines.

inferences.inference: Growth is constrained by web presence, not by capability.
inferences.reasoning: Forty-plus years of equipment and four production lines versus a home page that states no services, no town, no hours and no call to action - the shop's searchable surface is a 2022 GoDaddy site with no service pages and an unclaimed review profile.

data_gaps: Google review count could not be read: the signed-out Maps profile shows only the 3.7 average ('limited view'), and full review text needs sign-in - not attempted.
Yelp page could not be confirmed or read (search returned no Yelp URL; direct Yelp fetch returned no content).
The Loc8NearMe 'more comments' page returned HTTP 403, so only three recent review excerpts were reviewed; complaint themes are unverified.

No employee count, revenue, square footage, equipment list or fleet data published; the LeadIQ firmographic page (2-10 employees, $1M-10M revenue, AWS/Microsoft 365 tech stack) looks auto-generated and is unverified - not used as fact.
No job postings found on Indeed, ZipRecruiter, Glassdoor or the company site; /careers is a 404.
Google web search was blocked by a bot check, so local news coverage beyond the sources listed could not be swept.
No Facebook, Instagram or LinkedIn page could be verified, so social activity and any growth announcements are unknown.
Whether the shop ever re-applied for NJ prescription-blank vendor authorization after the 2019 eligibility date is unknown; it is simply absent from the current list.
LoopNet listing for 46 Paterson St. returned HTTP 403, so no lease/sale or building-size detail was obtained.
Phone-only details (after-hours voicemail, call answering) could not be checked without calling, which is out of scope.
The NJ Consumer Affairs press release page for the 2016 action (njconsumeraffairs.gov/News/Pages/06012016.aspx) was blocked by a bot wall, so only the consent-order PDF itself was used.
